meanings.note: Adverbial form of あまり.

examples.text: あまりに突然で驚いた。
examples.trans: It was so sudden that I was surprised.

examples.text: あまりに美しくて言葉が出ない。
examples.trans: It's so beautiful that I'm speechless.

meanings.note: Humble counterpart of もらう; volitional いただこう means 'let's take them / I'll have them'.

forms.title: Key forms of いただく

examples.text: お時間をいただけますか。
examples.trans: Could you spare me some time?

meanings.note: Conversational interjection.

examples.trans: Oh dear, we're in a bind.

meanings.note: Turns a statement into a question, or softens a volitional/negative guess.
Follows a clause to give a reason or reassuring explanation.

examples.trans: Because it is close, I walk.

meanings.note: Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

meanings.en: do a favor for the speaker
meanings.note: After a te-form (会ってくれる？), warmly asks 'will you do that for us?'

examples.trans: Will you come again for me?

examples.text: 母が料理を作ってくれました。
examples.trans: My mother cooked food for me.

meanings.note: Standard polite 'goodbye'.
Auxiliary godan verb following て-form.

examples.text: つい忘れてしまいました。
本を全部読んでしまった。
examples.trans: I finished reading the whole book.

meanings.note: Plain い-adjective.

examples.text: 彼の英語は本当にすごい。

meanings.note: All-purpose action verb; turns Sino-Japanese nouns into verbs (融通する, 出店する) and with に means 'decide on' or 'make into'.
In casual speech, それ plus は often fuses into そりゃ ('well, as for that / of course').
Plain sentence-ending copula; contracts or shifts to だった in past, だろう/だろ for supposition, and で/じゃ in combinations.
Limits the preceding noun or phrase to that item alone.

examples.text: これだけお願いします。

meanings.note: Polite sentence-ending counterpart of plain だ.

cells: ではありません / じゃありません

meanings.en: whichever (after question word); or something like
meanings.note: After どれ (どれでも) means 'any one at all'; after a noun (店でも) suggests an example ('a shop or something').

examples.text: いつでも来てください。
お茶でも飲みませんか。
examples.trans: Won't you have tea or something?

meanings.note: Asks about condition, outcome (どうだった), or what happened (どうしましたか).

meanings.en: what kind of; what sort of
meanings.note: Interrogative prenominal modifier.

examples.text: どんな音楽を聴きますか。
examples.trans: What kind of music do you listen to?

examples.text: どんな仕事をしているんですか。
examples.trans: What kind of work do you do?

なら.gloss: if it is; in the case of

meanings.note: Conditional topic marker placed right after a noun or pronoun (あなたなら 'if it were you').

examples.text: あなたならどうしますか？
examples.trans: If it were you, what would you do?

examples.text: 明日なら時間があります。
examples.trans: If it is tomorrow, I have time.

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.
Checks agreement ('isn't it?') or softens a request or farewell.
Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).
Conjunctive particle giving a reason, softer than から.

examples.text: 雨が降っているので、家にいます。
examples.trans: Since it's raining, I'm staying home.

examples.text: 時間がないので急ぎましょう。
examples.trans: We don't have time, so let's hurry.

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.
Replaces は, が, or を to add 'also' or 'too'.

examples.trans: Please give me this one too.

examples.text: あそこも新しい店です。
examples.trans: Over there is a new shop too.

meanings.note: Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.
Written を and pronounced o; marks what an action directly acts upon.
Loanword from English 'special', used as a na-adjective.

examples.text: 今日はスペシャルな日です。
スペシャルなサービスをご用意しました。
examples.trans: We have prepared a special service.

meanings.note: Loanword from English 'sales'.

examples.text: これからセールスに行きます。
examples.trans: I'm going out on sales calls now.

examples.text: セールスの仕事は大変です。

meanings.note: Playful loanword transliteration of English 'beautiful'.

examples.text: 今日の夕日はビューティフォーだ。
ビューティフォーな景色ですね。

meanings.note: Na-adjective (じょうず).

examples.text: 日本語がとても上手ですね。

examples.trans: You're good at flattery, aren't you?

meanings.note: Read なん before だ/です/の, and なに before が/を or alone.

examples.text: 何を買いにきましたか。
examples.trans: What did you come to buy?

meanings.note: Used among friends and peers by men; switch to 私 or 僕 in formal settings.
Godan verb: potential polite 入れます (はいれます) means 'can enter'.

examples.text: 予約なしでも入れますか。
examples.trans: Can we get in without a reservation?

meanings.note: Noun.

examples.text: 新しい商品を開発しています。
examples.trans: We are developing a new product.

examples.text: この商品はとても人気があります。

meanings.note: Noun (いえ).

examples.text: 駅の近くに新しい家を建てた。
examples.trans: I built a new house near the station.

examples.text: 今日はずっと家にいます。
examples.trans: I'll be at home all day today.

meanings.note: Noun.

examples.text: 英語の教材を買いました。
分かりやすい教材を使う。

meanings.note: Adverbial form 早く urges someone to hurry up.

examples.trans: I woke up early in the morning.

meanings.note: Na-adjective.

examples.text: 行けなくて本当に残念です。
examples.trans: It's really a shame that I can't go.

examples.text: それは残念なお知らせですね。

meanings.note: Na-adjective.

examples.text: 特別な理由はありません。

meanings.note: After なくて (隠さなくて結構です), politely says 'there is no need to'.

examples.text: 明日は来なくて結構です。
examples.trans: You do not need to come tomorrow.

meanings.note: Compound noun.

examples.text: 毎週英会話の教室に通っています。
examples.trans: I attend an English conversation class every week.

examples.text: 英会話の教材を探しています。
examples.trans: I'm looking for English conversation study materials.

meanings.note: Covers everything from a casual chat to a business deal or idea.

examples.trans: Let us have a little talk.

meanings.note: Godan verb.

examples.text: そのニュースを聞いて驚きました。
examples.trans: I was surprised to hear that news.
I was startled by the loud noise.
